The gateway setting that allows media to skip Microsoft’s processors. It is not implied by a short ping. Why it matters: Leave it off until the path is drawn.

cards.front: How do you approach Media bypass flag?
cards.back: Set it on the paired gateway, then test from the real subnet. If it fails: It is enabled tenant-wide in someone’s notes and only one site can route to the SBC.
The default media path through Microsoft media processors in the region closest to the call. Why it matters: Use it when bypass is unsafe.

cards.front: How do you approach Processor path?
cards.back: Allow the documented UDP ranges. If it fails: Bypass is off and those ranges are still closed, so audio never starts.
Media processors exist in multiple regions. Calls prefer a close one. You do not pick a street address for the processor. Why it matters: A hairpin to a distant egress undoes that preference.

cards.front: How do you approach Region of media?
cards.back: Keep egress local. If it fails: European users egress in another continent and RTT follows.

A user can be licensed and still not be enabled for Enterprise Voice in the way the tenant expects. Read the user before you test. Why it matters: The symptom is a client that never offers a dial pad.

cards.front: How do you approach Voice user disable?
cards.back: Read the voice attributes and the license together. If it fails: The dial pad is missing and the SBC is rebooted.
A Teams calling policy controls client calling features. It is not the voice routing policy that selects an SBC. Why it matters: Two policies with similar names get granted backwards.

cards.front: How do you approach Calling policy?
cards.back: Grant the routing policy and the calling policy on purpose. If it fails: Outbound PSTN is blocked by a calling policy and the route is blamed.
Presenting a service number instead of a personal mobile. It is a policy, not a hope. Why it matters: Wrong caller ID breaks return calls and CRM trust.

cards.front: How do you approach Caller ID substitution?
cards.back: Set it on the user or the resource account you mean. If it fails: Customers call back a personal mobile that was never the company number.
Teams translations use tokens such as $1 for a capture group. The first matching rule applies the translation and stops. Why it matters: A $1 with no group copies nothing useful.

cards.front: How do you approach Normalization translation tokens?
cards.back: Test the rule with the raw digit string. If it fails: The translation says +1$1 and the pattern never captured a group.
A short rule can turn a 4-digit extension into E.164. It must not run before emergency codes. Why it matters: Extensions and short codes share a length problem.

cards.front: How do you approach Extension dialing?
cards.back: Order the rules and test 112, 999, 911, and an extension. If it fails: 112 becomes an extension and leaves via the wrong trunk.
The attendant’s holiday set replaces business hours for those dates. Why it matters: Next year’s holidays are a December project.

cards.front: How do you approach Holiday call flow?
cards.back: Load them when you build the attendant. If it fails: The office is closed and the queue still rings.
The attendant’s operator is where zero, and many failures, should land. Why it matters: An attendant with no operator drops people who do not match a menu.

cards.front: How do you approach Operator zero?
cards.back: Name a person or a queue. If it fails: Callers who press nothing are disconnected.
Directory search should list only the people you intend callers to reach. Why it matters: A wide directory publishes privileged accounts.

cards.front: How do you approach Dial by name scope?
cards.back: Scope it. If it fails: A caller reaches an executive because search was unrestricted.
Serial routing uses the order of the agent list. Round robin does not. Why it matters: The person on top of a serial list takes the punishment.

cards.front: How do you approach Agent list order?
cards.back: Pick the method that matches the promise to the team. If it fails: One agent receives every call and the others look idle.
How long the caller waits before overflow. Too short and overflow is the product. Too long and they abandon. Why it matters: Test with agents busy.

cards.front: How do you approach Queue timeout seconds?
cards.back: Set it in the queue and call it. If it fails: Timeout is a few seconds and nobody is ever answered.
The audio file must be one you have the right to play. A popular song is not a free hold track. Why it matters: Licensing the song is a legal problem, not a Teams setting.

cards.front: How do you approach Greeting rights?
cards.back: Use a file you own or have licensed. If it fails: A commercial track is uploaded as hold music.
Where calls go when the attendant is closed. Voicemail, another number, or a message. Why it matters: Closed with no target is a hang-up.

cards.front: How do you approach After hours target?
cards.back: Set it and call after hours, or fake the schedule in a lab. If it fails: Night calls ring the daytime queue.
A named place in the Teams network topology. Subnets attach to it. Emergency addresses and LBR attach to that story. Why it matters: A site with no subnets does nothing.

cards.front: How do you approach Network site object?
cards.back: Create the site, then the subnets, then the address. If it fails: The address exists and no subnet points at it.
Civic addresses are validated. An unvalidated string is not a location you can trust. Why it matters: A typo in the street number sends responders next door.

cards.front: How do you approach Emergency address validation?
cards.back: Validate, then test from a known subnet. If it fails: The address was typed and never validated.
Wi-Fi clients can roam across subnets that do not match the building you think. The subnet you mapped is the location you will send. Why it matters: A café SSID bridged to HQ is a false floor.

cards.front: How do you approach Wireless location caution?
cards.back: Map only networks you control. If it fails: Guest Wi-Fi is inside the HQ subnet.

Clients must be able to use the appliance when the cloud path is gone. An appliance with no client configuration is a spare server. Why it matters: Read the current SBA article for how clients select it.

cards.front: How do you approach SBA registration?
cards.back: Test with the WAN blocked, from a phone on that site. If it fails: The appliance is powered on and no client knows it.
The SBA still needs a PSTN path. That is the local SBC and carrier, not a cloud media processor you cannot reach. Why it matters: Survival without a local trunk is a slogan.

cards.front: How do you approach Local SBC during survival?
cards.back: Prove a PSTN call with the WAN down. If it fails: The WAN test blocks Microsoft 365 and the only carrier path was through that same WAN.
Rooms need the same DSCP plan as PCs, using the rooms guidance for Windows and Android. Why it matters: A room that sounds worse than a laptop is often unmarked.

cards.front: How do you approach Teams Rooms QoS?
cards.back: Include the room subnet in the ACL. If it fails: Only user PCs were marked.
The phone signs in as its own account. Voicemail and caller ID follow that account. Why it matters: A shared PIN on a former employee’s account is a privacy incident.

cards.front: How do you approach Common area identity?
cards.back: Create the device account and the number. If it fails: The hallway phone opens a person’s mailbox.
A policy that requires a compliant interactive PC will block a phone or a room. Why it matters: The failure looks like a bad password.

cards.front: How do you approach Device conditional access?
cards.back: Scope a device path you can explain. If it fails: Rooms fail on Monday after a security baseline.
Certification is specific about software. ‘We own AudioCodes’ is not a version. Why it matters: Upgrade without checking the list can move you off support.

cards.front: How do you approach Firmware on the list?
cards.back: Record the version next to the list date. If it fails: The SBC was upgraded on Friday off the certified train.
Both sides must agree the media is SRTP. A gateway forced to RTP/AVP will not complete a normal Direct Routing call. Why it matters: Silence or a failed offer follows.

cards.front: How do you approach SRTP profile mismatch?
cards.back: Capture SDP and read the profile. If it fails: The carrier leg is SRTP and the Teams leg was stripped.
The SDP way digits are carried so an IVR can see them even when the audio codec would hide tones. Why it matters: In-band tones through a lossy codec disappear.
Offer telephone-event and test a digit. If it fails: The bot never hears 1 and the talk path is fine.
The header that stays with a SIP dialog so two logs can be proved to be one call. Why it matters: Timestamps collide.

cards.front: How do you approach Call-ID header?
cards.back: Copy it into the ticket and the CRM. If it fails: Two engineers compare two different INVITEs.
Who the request claims to be, and who it is for. A normalization bug shows up here as a duplicated country code. Why it matters: Read them before you read codecs.

cards.front: How do you approach From and To headers?
cards.back: Compare them to the dialed E.164. If it fails: The To header contains +4444… and the carrier rejects it.
The media description inside the INVITE when early offer is used. Codecs, ports, and SRTP live here. Why it matters: A 488 is an SDP argument.

cards.front: How do you approach SDP offer?
cards.back: Read the offer and the answer. If it fails: The offer lists a codec the other side rejected.

A commonly taught CQD clue is to treat sustained jitter around 30 ms as painful. Confirm the current data dictionary before you quote a threshold as policy. Why it matters: The clue is a starting point, not a statute.

cards.front: How do you approach Jitter over 30 ms teaching clue?
cards.back: Pair the number with DSCP and the path. If it fails: A ticket cites a threshold and nobody captured the packets.

Packet loss near 10 percent is a widely used teaching line for a poor stream. Verify the current CQD definition before you automate an alert on it. Why it matters: Loss and jitter are different faults.

cards.front: How do you approach Loss around 10 percent?
cards.back: Look at loss separately from RTT. If it fails: Bandwidth is added for a path whose loss is near zero and whose RTT is 600 ms.
CQD’s subnet field is only useful if you built the building map from real subnets. Why it matters: A typo relocates a building.

cards.front: How do you approach Subnet dimension?
cards.back: Reconcile with the emergency list. If it fails: 10.8.0.0/16 is named Headquarters.
The unit unified routing assigns: a call, a chat, a case. It is not a Teams message. Why it matters: Capacity is counted in work items.

cards.front: How do you approach Work item?
cards.back: Watch one test item cross classification. If it fails: Items vanish because no queue will accept them.
Representatives receive work only from queues they belong to. Why it matters: A license without membership is a spectator.

cards.front: How do you approach Queue membership?
cards.back: Add the person to the queue and set capacity above zero. If it fails: The queue has users and still overflows.
The Dataverse role that lets a representative open the app and touch the rows they should. Why it matters: Teams admin is not this role.

cards.front: How do you approach Security role in Dynamics?
cards.back: Assign the contact-center role the current guide names. If it fails: The user sees a blank console.
Contact Center can sit inside Customer Service or stand as its own app. Agents must be told which one they open. Why it matters: The pilot URL is not tribal knowledge.

cards.front: How do you approach Embedded versus standalone?
cards.back: Write the URL and the mode in the design. If it fails: Agents look in the wrong app and report an outage.
The classification result you get when the model or the rules do not know. It needs a queue. Why it matters: A loop is not a bucket.

cards.front: How do you approach Intent unknown bucket?
cards.back: Route unknown to humans. If it fails: Unknown replays the same prompt.
A draft of the conversation for the representative. It can be wrong. The representative still owns what is sent. Why it matters: A wrong summary in the case file becomes the record.

cards.front: How do you approach Copilot summary?
cards.back: Test on a known case. If it fails: The summary names the wrong product and is saved.
The date on the source the bot is allowed to quote. Retired prices stay retired only if you remove them. Why it matters: Grounding in a stale library is confident nonsense.

cards.front: How do you approach Knowledge article freshness?
cards.back: Review sources on a schedule. If it fails: The bot quotes last year’s fee.
The classic-topic path when nothing else matches. Empty fallback is silence. Why it matters: Write a sentence and an escape.

cards.front: How do you approach Fallback topic?
cards.back: Test an utterance you did not train. If it fails: The caller hears nothing after a novel sentence.
The usual human escape. It has to be implemented, not merely printed on a slide. Why it matters: Test it after every prompt edit.

cards.front: How do you approach DTMF zero?
cards.back: Press 0 in the lab and in production pilot. If it fails: The prompt mentions zero and the recognize step ignores it.
The Teams user who receives a PSTN transfer needs Teams Phone and a number in the Connect model’s description. Why it matters: Chat-only experts cannot take the call.

cards.front: How do you approach Transfer target license?
cards.back: License the humans on the transfer list. If it fails: Finance is chat-only and every transfer fails.
Some Connect providers share SBC infrastructure across customers. Your routing must still isolate your numbers. Why it matters: A shared SBC is not a shared dial plan.

cards.front: How do you approach Multitenant SBC caution?
cards.back: Confirm the provider’s isolation story. If it fails: A test number lands in another customer’s tenant.
The carrier document that allows a number to move. Porting without it does not happen. Why it matters: A weekend cut that assumes the port is done will strand the number.

cards.front: How do you approach Letter of authority?
cards.back: Confirm the port date in writing. If it fails: Both carriers route the number on Monday.
The old path left in place so numbers can return. Deleting it is not a cleanup. It is the removal of the safety. Why it matters: Keep it until the new path has a quiet week.

cards.front: How do you approach Rollback route?
cards.back: Write the backout steps. If it fails: The maintenance window ends with no public route.
Many Teams policies, including compliance recording, can target a group. Membership changes the effective policy without a click on the user. Why it matters: A contractor group can inherit recording.

cards.front: How do you approach Group policy assignment?
cards.back: Read the effective policy after group changes. If it fails: Recording starts for people who were only added to a mail group.
Teams Phone subscriptions include a number of free resource-account licenses you still have to acquire in the admin center. Why it matters: Free does not mean already present.

cards.front: How do you approach Zero-cost allotment?
cards.back: Buy the zero-price SKU and assign it. If it fails: Queues are built before any resource-account license exists in the tenant.

The prerequisite article says the tenant needs Teams Phone licensing for the voice-app services to exist. Why it matters: A tenant with only resource accounts and no phone-system license will not behave.

cards.front: How do you approach At least one Teams Phone?
cards.back: Confirm a real Teams Phone license exists. If it fails: The first queue is created in an empty tenant and never answers.
A shared Global Administrator account erases the audit of who changed a route. Why it matters: Named accounts, voice roles.

cards.front: How do you approach Do not share global admin?
cards.back: Remove shared admin use from the voice runbook. If it fails: The SBC password and the global admin password are the same note.
Use 555 numbers and example domains in labs. They are not a customer directory. Why it matters: Find-and-replace onto a real tenant is how labs become incidents.

cards.front: How do you approach Sample 555 numbers?
cards.back: Keep lab names obvious. If it fails: A practice script targets production.

A certification you forget to renew expires for you. A retirement means Microsoft withdrew the exam. They are different calendars. Why it matters: MS-700 can lapse in your transcript and still be a live exam for others.

cards.front: How do you approach Renewal versus retirement?
cards.back: Renew on Learn. Check the retirement list separately. If it fails: Someone says MS-700 is retired because theirs expired.
Microsoft’s practice questions, when published, match the exam more honestly than a random PDF. Why it matters: AB-250’s page has warned that the practice assessment may lag the live exam.

cards.front: How do you approach Official practice assessment?
cards.back: Use it if it exists, and still read the study guide. If it fails: A third-party dump is the only study tool.
The half hour you staff, not the daily average divided into imaginary hours. Why it matters: Erlang inputs are interval math.

cards.front: How do you approach Busy-hour interval?
cards.back: Export that interval. If it fails: The link is fine at noon and dead at 09:15.
Whether the agent was in the state the schedule promised. It needs a real state feed from the contact center. Why it matters: Teams presence is a weak substitute for contact-center state.
Feed the contact-center state to WFM. If it fails: Agents look available in Teams during after-call work.
A pair: a percent and a number of seconds, plus the abandon rule. ‘Eighty twenty’ means nothing until both are defined. Why it matters: Write it down.

cards.front: How do you approach Service level target?
cards.back: Use the same definition in the report and in Erlang. If it fails: Two dashboards disagree and both claim victory.
The hold file is a copyrighted work unless you made it or licensed it. Why it matters: Uploading a song is not a technical setting.

cards.front: How do you approach Hold music licensing?
cards.back: Use a track you can defend. If it fails: A famous song plays to every caller.
The people the emergency policy emails or messages when an emergency call starts. Why it matters: An empty group is a silent policy.

cards.front: How do you approach Notification group?
cards.back: Put facilities or security in it and test. If it fails: Responders arrive and nobody inside knows which floor.
A location specific enough for a responder to find the caller. A city name is not enough for a campus. Why it matters: Floors and suites matter.
The number or process the carrier gave you for emergency tests. It is not the public emergency number. Why it matters: Curiosity calls to the real service are how you meet the police and a fine.
VPN configuration that sends only corporate apps through the tunnel and lets Teams media go direct. Why it matters: Full tunnel is the opposite.
A switch copy of packets so you can see DSCP at the egress without standing on the user’s keyboard. Why it matters: The proof of QoS lives there.
A router rule that sets DSCP based on the port range, useful for devices that will not mark for themselves. Why it matters: Combine it with client marks where you can.
A call has media each way. Sizing one direction and forgetting the other undersizes a symmetric policer. Why it matters: State which number you quoted.
G.722 at 160 bytes every 20 ms pays the same header tax as G.711. Wideband does not remove IP headers. Why it matters: Do not quote 64 kbit/s as the link budget.
Silence suppression lowers the average and not the peak. Size the peak. Why it matters: A quiet average hides an all-hands call.
A quiet week on the new path before you delete the old trunk. Why it matters: Friday-night deletion is not a cleanup task.
Move people who call each other in the same migration wave so they do not trombone for a year. Why it matters: Tromboning is a cost.
Contact-center numbers stay on UCCE. User numbers go to Teams. The SBC enforces the split. Why it matters: One route pattern that sends everything to Teams strands the IVR.
Supervisor features such as whisper and barge belong to the contact-center product, not to a Teams peer call. Why it matters: Do not promise them from a Teams calling policy.
If the contact center and Teams both record, you still need one Call-ID to know it is the same conversation. Why it matters: Two audio files without a key are two rumors.
Recording, desktop capture, and directory search all need a privacy decision before go-live. Why it matters: A surprise recorder fails the review in public.
A retention setting you have never restored is a hope. Ask the recording partner for one file back. Why it matters: Legal hold on a mailbox does not do this.
Quality scores should use a form published to the people being scored. Why it matters: Secret criteria are not coaching.
Queue totals have to be able to leave the contact center on a schedule the WFM tool can read. Why it matters: A screenshot is not a feed.
If shrinkage is a guess, say it is a guess. Thirty percent is not a law of nature. Why it matters: Hidden assumptions become fights.
High occupancy next to rising abandons means the service level is being spent to look efficient. Why it matters: Watch both.
E.164, Call-ID, queue, agent. Four fields make a case auditable. Why it matters: A free-text note does not.
A list of utterances whose correct intent you already know. Run it before you publish a prompt change. Why it matters: Foundry is a place to do this. A phone number is not.
A design that needs a product Microsoft has not shipped is not a hook. It is a bet. Why it matters: Hooks in this campus use today’s policies, events, and identifiers.
The Direct Routing page that shows whether Teams considers the SBC healthy. Why it matters: It reflects OPTIONS and pairing, not your feelings about the carrier.
Inbound and outbound are different routes. A successful outbound call does not prove the carrier can deliver inbound. Why it matters: Always do both.
You care that the emergency call leaves, and that the location and notification are correct. Inbound to the queue is a different test. Why it matters: Do not mix the evidence.
Two dates that take companies down: the holiday the attendant does not know, and the certificate that expires. Why it matters: Put both on one calendar.
Contoso, Fabrikam, and 555 numbers in this campus are samples. They are not your tenant. Why it matters: Do not whois them and open a ticket.
14 October 2026 is when this campus was compared with Learn. It is not a promise the page stays still. Why it matters: Say the date when you quote a retirement.
